chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام about a house that belonged to a woman who had a son and a daughter. The son disappeared at sea, and the woman died. Her daughter claimed that her mother had assigned that house to her and had sold parts of it, and a portion remained in the house beside the house of a man from among our brothers. He disliked purchasing it because of the son's absence and because of what he feared, that purchasing it might not be permissible for him, while no news of the son was known.
He said: “And for how long has he been absent?” I said: “For many years.” So he said: “He waits through an absence of ten years, then he may purchase it.”

key_terms.أَشْقَاصًا: portions or shares of the property
key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, where the son was lost
key_terms.دَارٍ: a house or property under dispute
key_terms.غَيْبَةَ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ: a ten-year period of absence required before proceeding
key_terms.فَغَابَ: he disappeared and his whereabouts became unknown
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: it is not permissible in law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying property when one of the heirs has been missing for many years?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning property connected to a missing heir whose fate is unknown. Imam Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام instructs that ten years should pass from the disappearance before the purchase is made, reflecting caution in property rights and the protection of possible inheritance claims.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3883 - It is narrated from Ali bin Mahziyar who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far Al-Thani (as) about a house that belonged to a woman who had a son and a daughter. The son went missing at sea, and the woman died. The daughter claimed that her mother had transferred the ownership of the house to her and sold portions of it, leaving a remaining portion beside the house of one of our brothers.
This brother was reluctant to purchase it due to the absence of the son and the concern that buying it might not be permissible, as there was no news about the son.

Imam (as) asked: "How long has he been missing?"
I said: "For many years."
Imam (as) said: "He should wait for the son's absence for ten years, and then he may purchase it."
